task.description: Idiom/OTP/scope-creep gate on ELIXIR-DEV's REQ-205 implementation, plus the formal AC7 yaml_elixir dependency sign-off SECURITY-REVIEWER deferred to REVIEWER (WF-02 Step 2d).

ac7_dependency_signoff.rationale: Read design §4 in full and confirmed against the real mix.exs/mix.lock. This is a reasonable, low-risk, correctly-scoped addition: (1) no YAML parser existed anywhere in the dependency tree before this (confirmed by §0's own deps/0 audit, re-verified by reading mix.exs directly), so some library is genuinely needed, not optional; (2) yaml_elixir is a pure-Elixir wrapper around :yamerl with zero native/NIF build surface -- strictly lower-risk than the wasmex/lua precedent already accepted unconditionally in this same mix.exs; (3) scoped `only: :test` in deps/0 (confirmed by direct read) so it never reaches a :prod release, mirroring stream_data's existing only: :test entry rather than wasmex/lua's unconditional entries; (4) alternatives were genuinely considered and reasonably rejected in §4: raw :yamerl (lower-level, no benefit over the wrapper) and a hand-rolled parser (would itself be the scope-creep this requirement's own boundary section forbids, for a test-fixture-only need). mix.lock pins to 2.12.2, transitively depends only on :yamerl (also hexpm, no further transitive surface). No lib/letflow/ code depends on it -- grep confirms zero references outside test/. This closes AC7.
verification_performed: confirmed only: :test scoping in the actual file, not just the design's claim
confirmed zero references to YamlElixir/yaml_elixir outside test/

idiom_and_supervision.gen_statem_otp: N/A for this requirement -- no state-machine/process code is introduced; Seed and Runner are plain functional test-support modules with no process spawning, no GenServer/gen_statem. No crutch pattern present.
idiom_and_supervision.supervision: N/A -- no new supervised process, no spawn, no singleton. Runner.dispatch_api_step/4 exercises Letflow.Router.call/2 in-process via Plug.Test, the same convention test/letflow/routers/req078_supporting_routes_test.exs already uses; no isolation model is collapsed since no production process topology is touched.
idiom_and_supervision.idempotency_mechanism_seed_ex: Matches the design's specified shape and this codebase's own established idiom exactly: every seed_*/N function in test/support/simulation/seed.ex follows the same pre-check (list/lookup) -> create-if-absent -> conflict-branch-refetch-on-race pattern (seed_company/1's get_tenant_by_slug pre-check with with_existing_tenant_onboarding/retry_onboarding_lookup fallback; seed_one_user/2's find_user_by_username pre-check with refetch_user_or_error fallback; seed_one_group/3's find_group_by_name pre-check with refetch_group_or_error fallback; seed_process/3's get_active_by_name pre-check with refetch_process_or_error fallback). This is the same TOCTOU-safe idiom already used elsewhere in this suite's tenant-provisioning tests (per ELIXIR-DEV's own citation), applied consistently across all four entity kinds -- no inconsistency found.
idiom_and_supervision.list_users_list_groups_substitution_verd: SOUND. Verified by reading the real lib/letflow/identity.ex directly (not trusting the handoff's claim): get_by_username/2 (line 1571) and username_unique_conflict?/1 (line 1527) and group_name_unique_conflict?/1 (line 1257) are indeed `defp` -- confirmed module-private, unreachable from test/support/simulation/seed.ex as ELIXIR-DEV reported. list_users/2 (line 283) has the real signature `list_users(params, opts)` returning `{:ok, %{users: [User.t()], next_cursor: ...}}`, requires `params.page_size` (Map.fetch!), and filters via `filter_by_search` doing an ILIKE across username/display_name/email when `params.search` is set -- seed.ex's find_user_by_username/2 calls exactly `Identity.list_users(%{search: username, page_size: 500}, prefix: prefix)` and then does an exact client-side `Enum.find(users, &(&1.username == username))`, which is the correct way to get exact-match behavior out of a substring-search API, and page_size: 500 is safely larger than any fixture company's population. list_groups/1 (line 528) has the real signature `list_groups(opts)` (no params argument at all, unpaginated, returns `{:ok, %{groups: [...], total: ...}}`) -- seed.ex's find_group_by_name/2 calls `Identity.list_groups(prefix: prefix)` and matches `&(&1.name == name)` client-side, which is correct since list_groups/1 has no search filter of any kind (matches the moduledoc's own description of this fact). Both substitutions preserve the mechanism (pre-check + conflict-branch fallback) the design specified; only the pre-check's underlying query changed, exactly as seed.ex's own moduledoc states.
idiom_and_supervision.type_safety_note: No new class of invalid state was introduced by this requirement that a struct/@type/Ecto.Enum change would make unrepresentable -- Seed/Runner are test-support code operating over existing, already-typed production structs (Tenant.t(), User.t(), Group.t(), ProcessDefinition.t()). Scenario.t()/RunReport.t() are new structs but are themselves already typed with @type/@spec throughout runner.ex (precondition/step/expected_outcome typespecs, custom_predicate_fun() type). Not filing a docs/issues/ type-safety item for this requirement -- none of the four questions surfaced a representable-but-invalid-state gap.

scope_discipline.verdict: CLEAN. git diff --stat main...HEAD confirms only test/support/simulation/, test/fixtures/simulation/, test/letflow/simulation/, mix.exs, mix.lock, one lib/letflow/design/ doc, and handoffs/ changed. Zero lib/letflow/ production files, zero priv/repo/migrations/ files, no route or controller. Runner's `via: gui -> :deferred_to_s8` disposition and the explicit non-build of Letflow.Routers.SimulationTest are both scope-discipline wins, not creep -- the module actively documents the boundary it is declining to cross rather than building toward it speculatively.
scope_discipline.no_premature_abstraction: No behaviour, macro, or generic plumbing introduced ahead of what this requirement needs. Scenario/RunReport are plain structs sized to what AC4/AC5/AC6 require; custom_predicate/1's closed named-function-clause registry (only "always_true" defined) is explicitly NOT a data-driven dispatch table -- correctly avoids building a generic rule-engine ahead of REQ-206/207/208 actually needing more predicates, and the module's own comment states this rationale.

moduledoc_verification_ac6.verdict: MET, verbatim-in-substance as design §7 requires. Read the actual committed text in test/support/simulation/runner.ex (not the design doc's description of what it should say): point 1 (test-execution harness role, correctness gate over S4/S5/S6) is present; point 2 (explicit non-overlap with simulation_test.zig/scenario_runner.zig, citing both R-Co paths `src/api/routes/simulation_test.zig` and `src/simulation/scenario_runner.zig` by path, with the design-time-validation-vs-runtime-behavior distinction stated) is present; point 3 (confirms Letflow.Routers.SimulationTest's reserved route slot per lib/letflow/router.ex's own inventory table is not filled by this requirement) is present. All three required points are genuinely in the text, not merely gestured at.

dead_default_arg_check.verdict: CLEAN. Grepped ` \\ ` across test/support/simulation/, test/letflow/simulation/, and test/fixtures/simulation/*.exs -- zero matches. No default-argument pattern (this session's most recurring bug class) present in any new file.

ac1_disclosure_verification.verdict: ACCURATE AND CLEARLY MARKED -- not a REVIEWER judgment call on acceptability (RELEASE-VALIDATOR/ORCH's call per the task framing), only a verification that the disclosure matches the actual files. Every one of the 12 fixture files opens with a `# SYNTHETIC FIXTURE -- NOT ported from R-Co.` header comment (verified swiftroute/company.yaml directly; header text is consistent with the AC1 gap statement in step-02a's handoff) explaining the R-Co-unreachable constraint and stating in-file that AC1's literal 'ported from R-Co' requirement is not satisfied by that file. This is not silently passed off as real content anywhere. test/fixtures/simulation/fixture_shape_test.exs's own moduledoc states explicitly it is 'not AC1's diff-style comparison test' and its assertions (@company_expectations, @actor_ids maps) are hardcoded against the same synthetic values actually present in the fixture files -- confirmed by reading both the test file and swiftroute/company.yaml/org_structure.yaml side by side; the test is not fabricating an assertion against invented 'real' R-Co values, it is self-consistency-checking the synthetic data it ships alongside.

result.note_for_doc_updater: The get_by_username/2 defp-substitution defect class (design assumed a function was callable; it was actually private) is the same class already documented in anti-patterns.md for REQ-195, but is a distinct sub-class -- REQ-195's was an assumed-but-unverified *arity/parameter-list* mismatch, this one is an assumed-but-unverified *visibility* mismatch. Worth a fresh anti-patterns.md entry or an explicit cross-reference at Step 6 (DOC-UPDATER's call, not written here) since this is the second time in this session a design's 'confirmed present and callable' citation missed the private/public distinction.
